name: Ignorance veiling knowledge (ajñāna)
description: Knowledge is covered by ignorance, and by that creatures are deluded (5.15); when ignorance is destroyed by knowledge of the self, knowledge illumines the highest like the sun (5.16); the doubt in the heart is born of ignorance (4.42); the ignorant one perishes (4.40).

name: Lack of faith (aśraddhā)
description: The faithless one (aśraddadhāna), with the ignorant and the doubter, perishes (4.40); by contrast the one with faith gains knowledge (4.39).

name: Attachment to the fruits of action (phala-saṅga)
description: The unyoked one, attached to the fruit through the working of desire, is bound (5.12); the Lord has no longing for the fruit of action (4.14); the free one abandons attachment to the fruit (4.20) and does not depend on it (6.1).

name: Fear (bhaya)
description: Many free of passion, fear and anger reached the Lord's state (4.10); the meditating yogin is without fear (6.14); the sage free of desire, fear and anger is forever free (5.28).

name: The pairs of opposites (dvandva)
description: The pairs such as cold and heat, pleasure and pain, honour and dishonour (6.7); one who has gone beyond them is not bound though acting (4.22); one free of them is easily released from bondage (5.3).

name: Aversion (dveṣa)
description: The constant renouncer is one who neither hates nor craves (5.3).

name: Excess or deficiency in eating and sleeping
description: Yoga is not for one who eats too much, nor for one who does not eat at all, nor for one given to too much sleep, nor for one who keeps awake (6.16).

name: Stain, impurity (kalmaṣa)
description: Impurity is destroyed by sacrifice (4.30), shaken off by knowledge (5.17) and destroyed in the seers who attain brahma-nirvāṇa (5.25); the yogin who has become Brahman is stainless (6.27–28). Cf. 'fault' (kilbiṣa), not incurred by the one without possessions (4.21) and cleansed in the striving yogin (6.45).

name: Desire (kāma)
description: Desire is absent from the undertakings of the wise (4.19); acting from desire, attached to fruit, one is bound (5.12); the surge of desire and anger is to be withstood before leaving the body (5.23); desires born of intention are to be abandoned without remainder in meditation (6.24); those free of desire and anger attain brahma-nirvāṇa (5.26).

name: Anger (krodha)
description: Anger, with desire, gives rise to a surge that the yoked one withstands before death (5.23); freedom from anger marks those near brahma-nirvāṇa (5.26), the ever-free sage (5.28) and the many who reached the Lord's state (4.10).

name: Restlessness of mind
description: Arjuna does not see how the yoga of sameness can stand steady because of restlessness (6.33): the mind is restless, turbulent, strong and obstinate, as hard to restrain as the wind (6.34); Kṛṣṇa agrees it is hard to restrain (6.35); it wanders off (6.26).
antidotes: bringing the mind back into the self wherever it wanders (6.26)

name: Envy (matsara)
description: The wise one, content with what comes by chance, is free of envy (vimatsara) and is not bound though acting (4.22).

name: Delusion (moha)
description: Knowledge taught by the truth-seers frees one from falling into delusion again (4.35); creatures are deluded because knowledge is covered by ignorance (5.15); the knower of Brahman is undeluded (5.20).

name: Passion (rāga)
description: Many free of passion, fear and anger, absorbed in the Lord, reached his state (4.10); the constant renouncer does not crave (5.3).

name: Doubt (saṃśaya)
description: The one whose self is doubt perishes, with neither this world nor the next nor happiness (4.40); doubt, born of ignorance and lodged in the heart, is to be cut by the sword of knowledge (4.41–42); Arjuna asks Kṛṣṇa to cut his doubt about the fallen yogin (6.39).

name: Contact-born enjoyments (saṃsparśaja bhoga)
description: The enjoyments born of contact are wombs of sorrow; they have a beginning and an end, and the wise one does not delight in them (5.22).
antidotes: non-attachment to external contacts and the happiness found in the self (5.21)

name: Attachment (saṅga)
description: Attachment is to be abandoned in acting (4.20, 4.23, 5.10, 5.11); the one ascended to yoga is attached neither to sense-objects nor to actions (6.4).

name: Intention (saṅkalpa) as bondage
description: Intention is absent from the undertakings of the wise (4.19); no one becomes a yogin without renouncing it (6.2); the one ascended to yoga has renounced all intentions (6.4); desires are born of intention (6.24).

name: The sense of 'I am the doer'
description: The yoked knower of reality thinks 'I do nothing at all', holding that the senses move among their objects (5.8–9); the lord creates neither agency nor actions nor their link with fruit — svabhāva acts (5.14). Chs. 4–6 do not use the compound kartṛtva-abhimāna.
